about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Ro Khanna

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: BAN DATA CENTERS IN RESIDENTIAL COMMUNITIES
statements.title: BAN DATA CENTERS IN RESIDENTIAL COMMUNITIES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, today, I am calling to ban data centers in residential communities and to ban Federal funding for Flock cameras.
We didn't fight a revolution to be ruled by tech billionaires.

Communities should have the right to say ``no'' to a data center being shoved down their throats, and we should have the right for women not to be surveilled by Flock cameras by rogue police officers.
As a Representative of Silicon Valley, I am calling for democratic accountability of this technology revolution.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT IS WINNING
statements.title: PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT IS WINNING
sentences: They are saying no to the unfair and lopsided economy that has allowed a few people to hoard extreme wealth and power, and they are saying yes to Medicare for All, to unions for all, to childcare for all, to making sure that we have a housing guarantee for kids by the time they are 35 if they work hard.
We stand for transforming this country for the working class over the billionaire class. ____________________
Elon Musk has been threatening to sue me or jail me, but I will tell you what: They should judge us by those who are attacking us.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GOVERNMENT AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY OF FEDERALLY FUNDED STATE- ADMINISTERED PROGRAMS ACT
statements.title: GOVERNMENT AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY OF FEDERALLY FUNDED STATE- ADMINISTERED PROGRAMS ACT
sentences: It directs the Government Accountability Office to conduct an independent review of Federal programs that States administer on behalf of working families.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FIGHTING BACK AGAINST DISMANTLING OF VOTING RIGHTS
statements.title: FIGHTING BACK AGAINST DISMANTLING OF VOTING RIGHTS
sentences: The gentleman spoke out and said that there was a case in the Supreme Court that is gutting the Voting Rights Act and that will take away from Black Americans the right to freely choose their Representatives.
A Supreme Court decision has been the fastest rollback of Black freedom and Black political rights since Rutherford Hayes ended Reconstruction.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SUPREME COURT ENGAGED IN UGLY RECIDIVISM
statements.title: SUPREME COURT ENGAGED IN UGLY RECIDIVISM
sentences: Mr. Speaker, the Supreme Court is engaged in an ugly recidivism to deny Black political representation in the South.
The moral light has been extinguished from the Supreme Court.
That is why we need term limits for Supreme Court Justices.
That is why we need to expand the Court from 9 Justices to 13 Justices, like we have 13 circuits.
Mr. Speaker, as we approach the 250th anniversary of our Nation, we need a modern Supreme Court to uphold our Nation's principles. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HELP AMERICAN PEOPLE REDUCE COSTS
statements.title: HELP AMERICAN PEOPLE REDUCE COSTS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, yesterday Secretary Hegseth couldn't answer my question about how much the war in Iran is costing the American people, so I am going to answer it for him.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RESTORE POWER TO THE PEOPLE
statements.title: RESTORE POWER TO THE PEOPLE
sentences: People feel they have no say while the rich and powerful call the shots.
First, appoint a special prosecutor to investigate and prosecute the Epstein class that abused and raped young girls.
Second, call a Constitutional Convention to overturn Citizens United.
This Congress isn't going to take on tech billionaires or private health insurance.
Go to the American people and have two-thirds of the States pass an amendment to overturn Citizens United, ban super-PACs and money in politics.
Third, ban the insider trading on Polymarket, Kalshi, and the stock market, where people have made millions because of this illegal, immoral war in Iran.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: END WAR IN IRAN
statements.title: END WAR IN IRAN
sentences: Mr. Speaker, this body needs to vote on Thomas Massie's and my resolution to end the war in Iran.
The President has sent 2,000 more soldiers from the Army's 82nd Airborne Division to Iran.
We cannot afford to put ground troops in Iran.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: COST OF THE WAR IN IRAN
statements.title: COST OF THE WAR IN IRAN
sentences: Mr. Speaker, the war in Iran is crushing the economy here at home.
Every day, we are spending $2 billion of American money in Iran.
To put that in perspective, for 20 days in Iran, we could have free public college for every American.
We could have childcare at $10 a day for working-class Americans.
Instead of putting more money into Iran, we need a Marshall Plan for the United States of America.
The Democrats stand for America's economy first, building jobs here, childcare here, and healthcare here.
Today, Senator Sheldon Whitehouse and I are introducing the Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act for oil companies.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIRECTING THE PRESIDENT PURSUANT TO SECTION 5(C) OF THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION TO REMOVE UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES FROM UNAUTHORIZED HOSTILITIES IN THE ISLAMIC REPU
statements.title: DIRECTING THE PRESIDENT PURSUANT TO SECTION 5(C) OF THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION TO REMOVE UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES FROM UNAUTHORIZED HOSTILITIES IN THE ISLAMIC REPUBLIC OF IRAN
sentences: We are seeing militarism erode the soul of our Nation, leading to a regime change war in Iran and utter human devastation in Gaza.
Today, this vote on Iran is not a procedural vote.

It is a vote to renew an America that leads once more through diplomacy, statesmanship, and principle, an America that strives to end cycles of violence rather than ignite them, an America that cooperates with other nations rather than bullying them into submission, an America committed to confronting child poverty, the climate crisis, and illiteracy, to advance our shared humanity, an America that is respected in the world again.
In this body, let us declare with courage and clarity that we reject this illegal and unjust war in Iran.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NO MORE MIDDLE EAST WARS
statements.title: NO MORE MIDDLE EAST WARS
sentences: That is why Congressman Massie and I will introduce a bipartisan Iran war powers resolution.
They want that money for manufacturing jobs here, for healthcare here, for childcare here, and for education here.
There is no doubt the Iranian regime is brutal in killing protestors and murdering their own people, but an American war will only inflame nationalism and will not prevent them from getting the bomb.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DECODING EPSTEIN FILES
statements.title: DECODING EPSTEIN FILES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, yesterday Congressman Massie and I went to the Department of Justice to read the unredacted Epstein files.
The reality is that Donald Trump's FBI scrubbed these files in March, long before Thomas Massie and I passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
The Epstein Files Transparency Act requires them to unredact those FBI files.

That means the survivors' statements to the FBI, naming rich and powerful men who went to Epstein's island, who went to his ranch, who went to his home and raped and abused underage girls or saw underage girls being paraded, are all hidden.
It is a blatant violation of the Epstein Files Transparency Act, but it also asks a fundamental question: Who are they protecting?
Why are they protecting these rich and powerful men, people I call part of the Epstein class?

Yet in the United States of America, we have someone in the Cabinet, Howard Lutnick, who is all over these Epstein files and who allegedly had business with Epstein after he was convicted of pedophilia, but is still in the Cabinet.
Are we going to call to account the rich and powerful people who broke the law or cavorted with a pedophile, a convicted pedophile?
Are we going to have prosecutions for billionaires who went to this island and either raped underage girls or saw underage girls being raped and didn't say anything?
Somehow, this country seems to be working for the rich and powerful; but it is not working for ordinary working-class Americans.
It is time to begin with accountability for the Epstein class.
Hold in front of Congress those people who visited the island or did business with Epstein after he was a convicted pedophile.
I will tell you what this is about.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: THERE CANNOT BE TWO TIERS OF JUSTICE IN AMERICA
statements.title: THERE CANNOT BE TWO TIERS OF JUSTICE IN AMERICA
sentences: Mr. Speaker, Thomas Massie and my Epstein Files Transparency Act led to millions of files being released that have shocked the conscience of the Nation.
Today, I call for Congress to hold in front of the Oversight Committee every single person who emailed about going to Epstein's island.
The American people are frustrated with the rich and powerful getting a different set of justice.
There cannot be two tiers of justice in America, and I will not rest until the people who committed these heinous crimes and this heinous behavior are held accountable. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 7006, FINANCIAL SERVICES AND GENERAL GOVERNMENT AND NATIONAL SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF STATE, AND RELATED PROGRAMS APPROPRIATIONS
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 7006, FINANCIAL SERVICES AND GENERAL GOVERNMENT AND NATIONAL SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF STATE, AND RELATED PROGRAMS APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026
sentences: When you have people in the MAGA base, when you have people like Joe Rogan talking about the lawlessness of a private police force--ICE acting as the President's private police force--then we know we have a crisis of freedom in this country.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEADLINE TO RELEASE EPSTEIN FILES
statements.title: DEADLINE TO RELEASE EPSTEIN FILES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, tomorrow at midnight is the deadline for Pam Bondi to release the Epstein files.
Now, three Federal judges have ordered the release of all of these files from Maxwell's and Epstein's grand jury.
We will not rest until the law is complied with and justice is served. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WE DON'T NEED ANOTHER REGIME-CHANGE WAR
statements.title: WE DON'T NEED ANOTHER REGIME-CHANGE WAR
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to sound the alarm on the military buildup in the Caribbean, edging us closer to a regime-change war in Venezuela.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF S.J. RES. 80, PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "NATIONAL PE
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF S.J. RES. 80, PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "NATIONAL PETROLEUM RESERVE IN ALASKA...
sentences: The Epstein class is going to go.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 5371, CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2026
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 5371, CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2026
sentences: Just today, it comes out that billionaires are worth $8 trillion.
Mr. Speaker, we need national health insurance in this country.
We need to tax billionaires in this country.
We need to stop funding Argentina and corrupt foreign leaders.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 4553, ENERGY AND WATER DEVELOPMENT AND RELATED AGENCIES APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.J. RES. 104,
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 4553, ENERGY AND WATER DEVELOPMENT AND RELATED AGENCIES APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.J. RES. 104, PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL...
sentences: This is an issue of 14-year-olds and 15-year-olds who told the stories of how they were solicited by Jeffrey Epstein and raped and assaulted.
Then they went to the police and the police didn't do anything because Jeffrey Epstein knew rich people, because he knew Presidents, because he knew donors.
I really don't understand why we are fighting over this.
Why don't we stand with these survivors and show this Nation we are still capable of coming together when it matters for truth and justice?

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MARKING 80 YEARS AFTER TRINITY, THE DANGERS OF NUCLEAR WAR HAVE NEVER BEEN HIGHER
statements.title: MARKING 80 YEARS AFTER TRINITY, THE DANGERS OF NUCLEAR WAR HAVE NEVER BEEN HIGHER
sentences: Even well-informed and dedicated advocates of halting the arms race are often reduced to arguing for fiscal responsibility.

The letter, organized by the Union of Concerned Scientists, explained that ``the US could eliminate the land-based leg of the triad tomorrow and the US public would only be safer for it.'' Progressives working to defund new weapons systems recognize that massive military spending is, in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., a ``demonic, destructive suction tube''--depleting enormous resources that should be devoted to meeting human needs instead of destroying lives and threatening human survival.

A less obvious problem is that the signers are not speaking out for vigorous American diplomacy to end the Ukraine war, which may be a prerequisite for restarting any semblance of dialogue on nuclear dangers between Washington and Moscow.
For more than three years, ever since the Russian invasion of Ukraine, congressional Democrats have rarely advocated the kind of diplomatic efforts that might stop the war's carnage.

But the default role for even progressive Democrats on the Hill has been to support no-strings arming of the Ukrainian military (``let's you and them fight'') while depicting the Kremlin as incapab]e of serious negotiations.

Yet the McGovern resolution says that the United States should lead a worldwide effort to prevent nuclear war by ``in particular, pursuing and concluding new nuclear arms control and disarmament arrangements with the Russian Federation to prevent a buildup of nuclear forces beyond current levels.'' So while some congressional Democrats are emphatic that the United States should directly negotiate with Russia to prevent nuclear war, those same lawmakers are not willing to push for US negotiations with Russia to end the Ukraine war.
The rote storyline--that Vladimir Putin is evil, end of story--blends in smoothly with US news media and the punditocracy.

Implicit in the current worldview is that-- after decades of war in Afghanistan and Iraq, causing deaths into the millions, and now while continuing to serve as the crucial accomplice for ongoing genocide in Gaza--the US government is clearly virtuous, in complete contrast with the Russian government because of its own unconscionable aggression in Ukraine, The prevailing reflex, to act as though US-Russia relations could roll along on two tracks--escalating geopolitical conflicts while restoring and concluding major nuclear-arms treaties--is the political equivalent of magical thinking, if not simply craven expediency.
Meanwhile, for the corporate beneficiaries of a trillion- dollar Pentagon budget and an out-ofcontrol nuclear weapons program, the more hostility toward Russia and China the better.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RELATING TO CONSIDERATION OF THE SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 4, RESCISSIONS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: RELATING TO CONSIDERATION OF THE SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 4, RESCISSIONS ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, the American people, Republicans, Independents, and Democrats want the Epstein files released with the victims' identity protected.
Congressman Massie and I introduced a bipartisan bill to release all the Epstein files and to make sure victims were protected.
Here is the problem: The grand jury testimony is largely about Epstein and Maxwell, not about all the rich and powerful men who abused, assaulted, and abandoned young women.

There are 10 Republicans who are on the side of the people and the children, but the entire Democratic Party is on that side and the Republicans have chosen to protect the rich and powerful men who have abused our children.
Now most people don't understand how this town works, so I am going to try to explain this really simply.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 4016, DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3633, DIGITAL ASSET MARKET CLARITY ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 4016, DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3633, DIGITAL ASSET MARKET CLARITY ACT OF 2025; PROVIDING FOR...
sentences: Mr. Speaker, last night, the Speaker's Rules Committee voted to block my amendment that called for the full release of the Epstein files while protecting the victims' identity.
A nation that chooses impunity for the rich and the powerful at the expense of children is a nation that has lost its moral purpose.
It is because these rich and powerful men donate to the politicians in Washington, D.C., and play golf with the elites in Washington, D.C. They are foreign leaders who we don't want to offend.
Or are you on the side of the rich and powerful who have had their thumb on the scales and shafted Americans for decades?

I hope people will find the courage of a Republican like Ralph Norman or a Republican like Marjorie Taylor Greene or a Republican like Thomas Massie or the many MAGA Republicans who are demanding the full release of the Epstein files.
It is not a question just of Epstein.
I hope everyone in this up-or-down vote will vote to make sure that the Epstein files are released while protecting victims' identity.
We are going to get a vote again this afternoon.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CALLING FOR THE RELEASE OF THE EPSTEIN FILES
statements.title: CALLING FOR THE RELEASE OF THE EPSTEIN FILES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I introduced today an amendment demanding the full release of the Epstein files.

Are we on the side of protecting the rich and the powerful who have put their thumb on the scales of government to suck out millions of dollars, while working- class Americans suffer, or are we on the side of the people?

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I never want to hear the Republicans lecture about fiscal responsibility again.

If you care about debt in this country, if you care about our grandkids being burdened with debt, if you care about a bond market devastation, then you need to recognize that this bill hurts America, and you need to support the Democratic plan for deficit reduction.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AMERICANS OF ALL PARTIES DO NOT WANT MORE WAR
statements.title: AMERICANS OF ALL PARTIES DO NOT WANT MORE WAR
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to oppose war in Iran or any wars of choice in the Middle East.
We need to be investing in good-paying jobs at home, healthcare at home, and childcare at home, not billions of dollars in missiles targeted at the Middle East that we can't afford.
The intelligence tells us that we just pushed Iran back 3 to 4 months in building a bomb.
Vice President Vance says they still have enough nuclear fuel to have 10 nuclear missiles.
We need tough diplomacy to deny Iran a bomb, not more wars at the expense of the American people.
That is why Representative Massie and I introduced a resolution to prevent more wars of choice.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ADDRESSING OUR EXPLODING DEFICIT
statements.title: ADDRESSING OUR EXPLODING DEFICIT
sentences: Now, Mr. Speaker, you say: How are we going to do this deficit reduction?
Where are the spending cuts, and where are the revenue generators?
Secondly, we need to go after negotiating with Big Pharma.
Medicare should be negotiating drug prices.
These are the big-ticket items that would actually start to reduce the deficit.
They always say that our side is not for spending cuts.
Right here are actual spending cuts of what we can be doing to reduce the deficit.
I never understood the billionaire argument.
I have more billionaires than anyone in this Chamber.
We should be making sure that we are taxing our stock buybacks.

We should be making sure that when we have large inheritances that people who are inheriting it actually have to pay capital gains so that we, in this country, start to reward hard work again and not just speculation.

Anyway, this plan would reduce the deficit, reduce debt by $12 trillion over 10 years, and it would also reduce the interest payments on the deficit every year which would add an extra $2 trillion of savings.

I hope, Mr. Speaker, we can come together in this body to be honest with the American people, to actually have a calculator to do math, and to propose real plans for deficit reduction. ____________________
So, today, we are introducing a plan, a real plan, to lower deficits in America.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TAX CUTS
statements.title: TAX CUTS
sentences: Here are the facts: We currently have about a $36 trillion debt, and we are spending right now $2 trillion more every year than we take in.
If you are a millionaire in America, you are going to get about $82,000 a year in tax breaks.
That is $82,000 of tax breaks for the millionaires, and $750 to working- and middle-class families.
By the way, the tax breaks for those millionaires and billionaires are permanent over 10 years.
Republicans say: No, for working families, we only want 4 years.
Tax breaks for the billionaires in my district in Silicon Valley, for those we want 10 years.
They are cutting $750 billion in Medicaid benefits.
Up to a million of American children, kids born in the United States, may lose their healthcare.
It is the largest cut to Medicaid in the history of this country, all to finance $96 billion a year of tax breaks to the millionaires and billionaires.
Even Donald Trump challenged the Congress to say: Raise taxes a bit on the rich.
We believe we should not be cutting Medicaid, essential healthcare services that help families, that support hospitals, and that support the health of so many seniors in this country.

I hope enough Republicans will say ``no'' to the tax breaks for the millionaires and billionaires, and will say ``no'' to piling on more debt which will raise interest rates, hurting our economic growth, exploding our trade deficit because of our reliance on foreign firms and foreign investment, and crippling ordinary Americans' ability to get loans.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: INTRODUCING LEGISLATION ON DRUG PRICING
statements.title: INTRODUCING LEGISLATION ON DRUG PRICING
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to introduce as legislation President Trump's executive order for the most-favored-nation status on drug pricing.

This executive order, codified by the legislation, will allow our Cabinet Secretaries to put pressure on Big Pharma and make sure that they are not price gouging and will allow for the importation of cheaper drugs.
The reality is that Big Pharma will sue over the executive order, like they did in the previous Trump administration.
The only way we can stand up to Big Pharma is to codify legislation, which the President wants to do in an executive order.
Are we going to stand in this body with the $16 billion that Big Pharma spent on lobbying, or are we going to stand with the American people?
Opposing Medicaid and NIH Budget Cuts Mr. Speaker, I rise today to oppose the cruel budget cuts on Medicaid and NIH.
The Republican budget would cut $715 billion from Medicaid.
It is going to mean that many hospitals won't be able to offer services in physical therapy and mental health counseling.
He said that these Medicaid cuts would be a total betrayal by the President and the Republican Party of the working class.
He was pretty clear that these cuts would be devastating for working families.

We used to have a bipartisan consensus in this country that we did not cut Medicaid, that we did not cut medical research, and that we did not give more tax breaks in my district in Silicon Valley, to the billionaires in my district, at the expense of medical research and the working class.
Mr. Speaker, I hope people in this body will reconsider the cruel cuts to Medicaid.

I hope people in this body will reconsider the cruel cuts to Medicaid, the cruel cuts to NIH, and tax the billionaires in my district a little more so we don't have to cut these essential programs. ____________________
We will know that answer based on how many cosponsors we get for my legislation that simply codifies Donald Trump's executive order.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MODERNIZING OUR ECONOMIC THEORIES
statements.title: MODERNIZING OUR ECONOMIC THEORIES
sentences: It means we are going to have to pay more on our debt.
They have tariffs at 1909 levels at 22.5 percent, making a global trade war.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ECONOMIC POPULISM
statements.title: ECONOMIC POPULISM
sentences: So one of the things this group wants to do is to renew economic revitalization in advanced manufacturing in these communities and to have a real plan for new semiconductors, new robotics, advanced steel, advanced automobiles, and have new factories and new industry come up.
The problem is they get here and their plan to solve this is to hand the reins to a number of headstrong billionaires who are libertarians.
Instead, they think that just having these billionaires cut deals with the private sector is going to help the working or middle class.
The genius lies not with billionaires and technologists.
We need a government that says: If you make it in America then we will buy it.
We need a government that says: If you skill the factories here we will help finance it.
We will make more money with AI.
I will tell you what it is not going to do, Mr. Speaker.
We are going to build this country back from the bottom up.
America needs to understand if we are going to innovate, then yes, we should innovate on technology, and yes, we should innovate on finance.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: BUDGET AND DEBT
statements.title: BUDGET AND DEBT
sentences: We have got a $36 trillion debt.
If you were to balance the budget, that would be zero and we should stay at a $36 trillion debt.
Their budget actually is going to add $28 trillion of debt over the next 10 years.
It is not just that they aren't balancing it to keep it at $36 trillion; it is that they are adding more debt by adding to the deficits more than the current deficits.
The current deficit projection would add $23.9 trillion of debt, but the Republicans want to add $28.5 trillion of debt, $4.6 trillion more of debt spending than the current deficit spending.

You want to deficit spend to have tax breaks for the wealthy because you think that will help the economy, fine, but every American should look at this chart because the Republican budget is making the deficit and the debt worse.

You can either come to Congress to explain this chart while you are going after 0.004 percent or USAID, which is 0.7 percent, as opposed to going to the 13 percent of the Pentagon budget while you are allowing tax breaks of 455 times more than the savings you are finding at DOGE--YOU can either come to Congress or you can go to Jon Stewart.
I will just go over some facts, not politically speaking, just facts.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MEDICAID CUTS MEAN HOSPITAL CLOSURES
statements.title: MEDICAID CUTS MEAN HOSPITAL CLOSURES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, the Republican budget calls for a trillion dollars in Medicaid cuts to pay for tax breaks for the very wealthy.
What do these Medicaid cuts mean?
They are taking away your Medicaid to line the pockets of the wealthiest Americans who are controlling our government. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: BAN ON ACCEPTANCE OF GIFTS FROM LOBBYISTS
statements.title: BAN ON ACCEPTANCE OF GIFTS FROM LOBBYISTS
sentences: This is going to impact over 12 million Americans, and the crazy thing is that the inspectors general have found that there is only 0.2 percent of fraud in telehealth.
Today, I am introducing the Drain the Swamp Act.
That is why I am introducing today the Telehealth Coverage Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECTING CIVIL SERVANTS
statements.title: PROTECTING CIVIL SERVANTS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, not since Abraham Lincoln suspended habeas corpus at the height of the Civil War has a President defied the United States Supreme Court.

Perhaps the Vice President doesn't know the history that Andrew Jackson's defiance of the Supreme Court led to the forcible removal of Native Americans and the Trail of Tears and shame for the country.
It is dangerous for him to call on the President to defy the Supreme Court.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: OUR GOVERNMENT MUST MAKE ECONOMIC INDEPENDENCE POSSIBLE FOR OUR CITIZENS
statements.title: OUR GOVERNMENT MUST MAKE ECONOMIC INDEPENDENCE POSSIBLE FOR OUR CITIZENS
sentences: That same challenge exists today, but now it is billionaires themselves taking over our government.
In their eyes, business entrepreneurs, hedge fund managers, and tech tycoons are the engines of America's prosperity, while working families are expected to accept whatever scraps trickle down.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ELIMINATING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION
statements.title: ELIMINATING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION
sentences: Mr. Speaker, NBC News is reporting that President Trump plans to eliminate the Department of Education with an executive order.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today to oppose Donald Trump's reckless tariffs on food products.
I am for strategic tariffs to protect our strategic industries in steel, aluminum, and semiconductors and our national champions.
We know, from Hamilton to Paul Krugman, that tariffs work for infant industries and important national industries, but who thinks we need tariffs for Corona beer?
Who thinks we need tariffs for vegetables?
Donald Trump put a 25 percent tariff on it.
We are in dangerous times where we have a President who could impose these tariffs on food at any moment.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: OPPOSE TIKTOK BAN
statements.title: OPPOSE TIKTOK BAN
sentences: We can protect Americans' data, we can protect us from foreign interference on algorithms, but we should not ban TikTok.
